samples.summary: No test for cut-paste of a merged block into a destination that overlaps the source
samples.evidence: The new code has an explicit branch for exactly this case — `applyPasteMerges` builds a `dropped` Map with the comment "A cut whose destination overlaps its source can name the same block twice; deleting it once is enough" (sheet.ts ~2447) — and `planPasteMerges` will also see the source block partially inside the shifted destination range, which would make it return `undefined` and refuse the whole cut. No test in the new `Sheet merge + copy-paste` block exercises an overlapping cut with a merge: 'should drop a cut merged block at the source' cuts A1:B1 and pastes at A3 (disjoint). The existing clipboard suite has an 'cut overlapping destination (A1:B1 from A1:B1, paste at B1)' case (packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts:596) proving this is a real user path, but it has no merges. So whether an overlapping merged cut moves, refuses, or leaves a dangling/duplicated merge entry is completely unverified.

samples.summary: The new `unblockedAnchors` / spill-cleanup plumbing on the paste path has no test
samples.evidence: `paste` now collects `unblockedAnchors`, adds them to `expanded` and seeds `dependantsMap` so blocked spill anchors re-attempt (sheet.ts 2323-2346), and `clearCellsUnderMerge` deletes spill ghosts and clears spill blockers for cells newly hidden by a pasted merge. No test creates a spilling formula or a spill-blocked anchor and then pastes a merge over it: grep for 'spill' across packages/sheets/test matches only worksheet-grid, formatting, calculation, data-validation, style-mutation and formula tests — none of them mention merge or paste (grep 'merge|moveRangeTo' in worksheet-grid.test.ts returns 0). A regression here would leave orphaned ghost cells or a permanently blocked spill.

`snapshotMergesIn` filters out blocks the copy range only clips (`filter((m) => isRangeInRange(m.range, range))`). Every new test copies either a whole merged block or a merge-free range, so the filter branch never fires — removing the filter would leave all new tests green while the copy buffer would carry a clipped block and re-create an out-of-range merge at the destination. The doc comment concedes the UI cannot reach it, hence minor, but the guard exists precisely for programmatic callers and nothing pins it.

samples.summary: Cut/replace paths assert only the in-memory merge map, never store deletion
samples.evidence: 'should persist the pasted merge to the store' checks `store.getMerges().get('A3')` for the created block, but no test checks that a dropped block (cut source, or a destination block the paste fully covers) is removed from the store — the cut test at line 400 and the 'drop a destination block' test at line 424 read only `sheet.getMerges()`, which is the in-memory `this.merges` map. If `store.deleteMerge` were skipped in `applyPasteMerges`, all these tests stay green and the stale merge would resurface on reload. Compare the drag-move suite, which does assert `stored.has('A1')` is false (merge.test.ts:163).

samples.summary: External spreadsheet-HTML paste over a merged block is untested
samples.evidence: The docstring claims all external pastes leave the merge layout alone, but only the plain-TSV branch is covered ('should leave the merge layout alone on an external paste' calls `paste({ text: '1\t2' })`, merge.test.ts:561). The `isSpreadsheetHtml(html)` branch (sheet.ts:2285), which is the branch a real Google Sheets/Excel paste takes, has no merge test.

samples.summary: `selectPastedRange` refactor to `rangeOf` has no assertion on post-paste selection
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites `selectPastedRange` to use `rangeOf(grid)`. Grepping packages/sheets/test for `getActiveCell`/`getRanges` shows matches only in sheet/sheet.test.ts selection tests, none following a `paste(` call (clipboard.test.ts has no selection assertions at all). A behavioural change here — e.g. wrong bounding box or lost `syncSelectionToPresence` — would not be caught. Pure refactor, so contained, but nothing pins the pre/post equivalence.

samples.summary: Style survival under a newly pasted merge is not asserted
samples.evidence: `clearCellsUnderMerge` deliberately preserves `cell.s` when clearing a covered cell (`await this.store.set(ref, { s: cell.s })`). 'should hide no stale data under a pasted merge' only checks the value is gone; no paste test writes a style on the covered destination cell and asserts it survives the merge, so the style-preserving branch is only distinguished from a plain delete by pre-existing move-path tests (which also do not assert it).

The existing clipboard suite has an 'cut overlapping destination (A1:B1 from A1:B1, paste at B1)' case (packages/sheets/test/sheet/clipboard.test.ts:596) proving this is a real user path, but it has no merges. verdict.reason: Verified the code branch exists and is untested. sheet.ts:2457-2468 has the explicit dedup for "A cut whose destination overlaps its source can name the same block twice", fed by the cut path at sheet.ts:2269-2281, while planPasteMerges (sheet.ts:2390+) can instead refuse the paste by returning undefined — two divergent outcomes, neither asserted anywhere. Repo-wide grep for `.cut(` shows only two test files exercise cut-paste: merge.test.ts and clipboard.test.ts. merge.test.ts's only cut case (line 386) cuts A1:B1 and pastes at A3, fully disjoint; every other case in the 'Sheet merge + copy-paste' block (lines 344-567) is a copy or an external paste. clipboard.test.ts does have overlapping cut cases (lines 596, 660) but contains zero occurrences of 'merge', so it cannot reach applyPasteMerges. I also checked co-located src tests, backend *.spec.ts, worksheet-keymap.test.ts, pivot-protection.test.ts, the concurrency test helpers, and packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-cut-paste.test.ts (which tests overlapping cut-paste but with no merges at all). No counterexample. The gap is blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: an unverified merge branch can ship a dangling or duplicated merge entry in both the in-memory map and the store on a real user path (cut a merged block, paste overlapping the source).
